biur-halacha/1:א: (א) Mean Dobby and so on, “Look at the U.S. and there is no negotiations in all this between men and women, a female model must all the things that belong to the arrangement as described above in the letter of the United States:
biur-halacha/1:ב: (ב) And they bless Birkat Hamazon for themselves, etc., and he finishes Hallel, etc. — the same applies that afterward he should also say to them "finish Hallel" and bless for them, and they drink the cup of Hallel [Levush and Pri Megadim].
eliyah-rabbah/1:_: (א) And he blesses for them Birkat Hamazon, etc. — for if he blesses for them he can no longer drink at home Birkat Hamazon (Tur in the name of Rav Amram); Beit Yosef and Taz strained in explanation — see their lengthy discussion; I found in Ra'avan 74 who concluded Rav Amram himself gave the reason Mar said between the third and fourth cups one should not drink — until here; meaning: when he blesses for them he must drink from the cup and it becomes his third cup, therefore Rosh enacted to prompt him word by word.
kaf-hachayyim/1:_: A. [Ps 119:105; 119:105; 119:105; 119:130] is the tongue of the Holy One, and the column as it is and the Old Testament, as it is, and also the Old Testament as it is.
rabbi-akiva-eiger/1:_: Seif 1: "and magid and they eat vegetables and matzah" — although he does not eat from the vegetable, nevertheless he can bless for them, since he is included by the Sages, as in the blessing on matzah — Rosh.
yad-ephraim/1:_: In Taz s.k. 3: "and he blesses for them Birkat Hamazon" — behold an enactment for those who know Birkat Hamazon; and if they do not know, Rav Amram wrote there is no [enactment], etc., as should be.
